title: Indicator lab
goal: Turn indicators on and off and say what each one shows.

objectives.text: Match each indicator to what it shows.
Tell an overlay from a strip under the chart.
Know why one indicator is not enough.

slides.text: An overlay is an indicator drawn on top of the candles. The SMA, EMA, VWAP and Bollinger Bands are overlays.
slides.title: Overlays

slides.text: RSI, MACD and volume get their own strip under the chart. Each strip has its own scale.
slides.title: Strips below

slides.text: Turn an indicator on to see it. Turn it off to hide it. Too many lines make a mess.
slides.title: On and off

slides.text: Each indicator shows just one thing. All of them use old prices. Use a few, and do not trust any one alone.
slides.title: Never alone

questions.prompt: Turn on SMA and Volume. Leave the rest off.
questions.explanation: The SMA is an overlay. Volume bars sit at the bottom.

questions.prompt: Turn on VWAP and Volume. Turn everything else off.
questions.explanation: VWAP needs an intraday chart. This one is.

questions.prompt: Turn on MACD. Turn off RSI.
questions.explanation: MACD and RSI both get a strip under the chart. Only MACD should stay on.

questions.prompt: Turn on RSI and Volume. Turn everything else off.
questions.explanation: You turned on two strips and turned off the two overlays.
A clean chart is a good place to start. Add one indicator at a time.

questions.prompt: Match each indicator to what it shows.

pairs.definition: The average of the last 20 closes
The average price of the day
Lines that open wide when prices swing

questions.explanation: The SMA sits on top of the candles. RSI and volume sit in strips below.

questions.prompt: Where does the RSI show up?

options.text: In a strip under the chart

questions.explanation: RSI has its own strip. It runs from 0 to 100.

questions.prompt: One indicator is enough to know what the price will do.
questions.explanation: No. All indicators use old prices. Use a few of them.
